title: River journey diagram
subject: Geography
unit: Summer 1: Rivers and the water cycle (Flow and One Planet, Our World)
source: Seeded from geography/y3 lesson 2 (River journey diagram (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 2: A river's journey from source to mouth. To understand how a river changes on its journey from source to mouth

picture.draw: Draw and label: River journey diagram

questions.model: I follow the river uphill. It gets smaller and smaller. Where it starts is the source.

questions.q: Is a river faster near the source or the mouth?
What is a big bend in a river called?
Label the river diagram with source, tributary, meander, estuary and mouth, and add arrows to show the flow.
questions.a: All five labels correct; arrows flow from source to mouth
questions.model: Teacher labels the source first and draws the first arrow.

questions.q: Write three sentences describing the river from source to mouth.
questions.a: For example: It starts as a small fast stream in the hills. Tributaries join it. It meanders slowly to the sea.

questions.q: Why does a river always flow downhill?
questions.a: Gravity pulls the water down towards lower land and the sea

questions.q: Where a river meets the sea is the:
Big question: why does a river flow downhill?
questions.a: Gravity pulls water from high land down to the sea
